Case study 07 · Salesforce · UX Framework & Redesign

Salesforce UX Framework /Redesign

Replaced a decade of agency-built pages with one framework, then made the forms convert.

Scroll the story

Role

UX Architect of the redesign and framework; later led the team

Timeline

2+ years hands-on, then managed

Team

VP executives, engineers, product marketing, content authors and researchers in three regions

−70%time authoring pages
+19%global conversion rate
+51%valid leads

The short version

01

The problem

Salesforce.com was built by many agencies, each with its own styles and navigation. The CRM leader’s first impression depended on which page you landed on.

02

What I owned

The information architecture, the component framework and a research practice run as an internal agency across AMER, EMEA and APAC.

03

The approach

Audited 36,000+ pages and retired most of them. Built the framework live without taking the site down, and collapsed about 20 navigation paradigms into one.

04

The result

Authoring time down 70%, conversion up 19%, valid leads up 51%. Stakeholders now pick from a catalog instead of commissioning one-offs.

01 — Strategy

Strategy

Strategy

Salesforce Design System

Goal:

Create a scalable system that can accommodate many uses cases both present and future. The design system would be modular and improve the overall consistency and user experience across all silos. Each component would be minimally customizable to still provide creativity with visual designers.

Strategy · Spaghetti Code / Systems / Processes

Spaghetti Code / Systems / Processes Pain points and challenges: • 200,000 pages & 6 different systems to consider • Tangled dependencies and legacy systems • No standardization + conflicting interaction patterns • Highly political & difficult to get buy in • Justification for funding was key

02 — Research

Research

Research

200,000 + Pages

Audits

The sheer scope of the project required months of in depth analysis of systems and use cases both WWW facing but the authoring environment and the usability of creation and reusability of components.

Research

The Best Of All Available

Not an exact fit..

We looked across the space to see what other frameworks provided and learn from the patterns that we would need to complete all the use cases we uncovered. Ultimately we took the best patterns from bootstrap and material design and built out the rest.

Research

Workshops & Stakeholder Interviews

Ensuring everyone is heard

With such a wide assortment

Research · Using Data To Prioritize

Competitive Analysis Content Audits User Interviews Surveys User Testing Using Data To Prioritize Looking across Silos With something of this size we knew it would take several years to accomplish it. Working with our analytics partners we developed a plan that minimized risk and ultimately cut down the amount of total pages.
